messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging sam (oncall): Elevated 5xx rate observed from gateway -> batching pathway. Cluster: us-east-1, svc: inference-gateway. Error spike started ~1767889950. Please ack and triage.

sam (oncall): Acked. looking. pulling logs.

opsbot: Automatically opened incident INC-2026-1767890000 and added severity: high. Notifying eng-sre and product-support.

maya: joining — seeing increased queue depth on scheduler nodes, lots of HOL blocking. backpressure metrics show batcher.queue_length up 8x.

lee-engineer: copying quick metrics: gateway 5xx p50->p95 jump, timeouts at gateway 504, internal 5xx (502/503). KV-cache evictions spiking. Could be runaway batch size causing long-running kernels.

sam (oncall): any customer-facing errors? ashley-support, do we have user reports?

ashley-support: yes — two enterprise customers reported elevated latency and timeouts in us-east. Support ticket numbers: SUP-8892, SUP-8893. Escalated to account team, customers warned we're investigating.

maya: quick mitigation idea: reduce max_batch_tokens per-model and enable preemptive eviction on oldest batches. I can push a throttle to batcher if we want immediate relief.

lee-engineer: +1 to throttling. also route small requests (seq < 64) to fast-path pool. large sequences appear to be monopolizing GPU contexts.

sam (oncall): do it. maya, run the throttle, and post commands. I'll coordinate customer comms.

maya: running commands now:
```bash
# reduce batch size and enable preemptive eviction
bin/infractl set-config --service=scheduler --key=max_batch_tokens --value=8 --env=prod-us-east
bin/infractl set-config --service=batcher --key=eviction_policy --value=oldest_first --env=prod-us-east
# lower batch assembly window
bin/infractl set-config --service=batcher --key=assembly_ms --value=10 --env=prod-us-east
```

maya: pushed. will take ~20s to take effect. watching queue.

lee-engineer: also enabling fast-path routing for short seqs:
```yaml
routing:
  - match: seq_length <= 64
    pool: fast-path-us-east
```

opsbot: Config change detected by deploy-bot: 3 config keys updated in prod-us-east. Rolling config reload started.

sam (oncall): monitoring logs, dashboard. any change in 5xx?

maya: partial improvement — queue depth dropping, head-of-line wait times down ~40%. 5xx rate trending down but still elevated (~3.8% -> 1.2%). Some gateway timeouts persist.

lee-engineer: setting temporary route fallback: send 20% of traffic to secondary region (us-west-2) for the next 30m to reduce pressure. Doing a gradual shift to avoid cold-start spikes.

maya: issuing route command:
```bash
bin/routectl set-weight --from=prod-us-east --to=prod-us-west-2 --weight=20 --duration=30m
```

opsbot: Traffic shift request queued. Confirm with rollout-bot?

sam (oncall): confirmed. rollout-bot, proceed.

opsbot: rollout-bot: traffic shift in progress: 0->20% over 2m.

ashley-support: letting customers know we routed some traffic to reduce impact. added note to SUP-8892 that we expect improvements in ~10-15m.

maya: note — discovered a batcher task stuck on a long kernel with huge seq-length caused by malformed user payload (no truncation). I've added a short-term guard to drop >4096 token requests with 429 and route to async pipeline.

lee-engineer: config to drop/async large requests:
```bash
bin/infractl set-config --service=gateway --key=max_seq_sync --value=4096 --env=prod-us-east
bin/infractl set-config --service=gateway --key=large_request_mode --value=async --env=prod-us-east
```

maya: pushed those too. immediate drops should free up processing.

sam (oncall): good call. any risk to correctness or customer SLA from dropping sync large requests?

ashley-support: enterprise customers on reserved dedicated pools unaffected; impacted are hosted API users. I'm drafting a status page update that clarifies dedicated customers are isolated.

lee-engineer: monitoring KV cache churn — eviction thresholds were too low, causing cache thrash. I bumped KVCACHE_SIZE for scheduler nodes +20% to reduce thrash.

maya: that helped with internal retries causing 5xx loops. 5xx down to ~0.6% now, timeouts largely resolved. queue length back to baseline in ~6m after changes.

sam (oncall): sweet. keep an eye for recurrence. next steps:
- run failure-correlation to find offending client payloads
- add a permanent limit for synchronous max_seq or auto-split large requests
- postmortem once stabilized (assign owner)

lee-engineer: I'll own the postmortem. tagging as lead: lee-engineer.

maya: I'll follow up with a change to batcher assembly logic to bias small requests and add more aggressive preemption for long-running kernels.

ashley-support: status page update posted: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/1767890000 — message describes mitigation and estimated recovery. customers updated.

opsbot: Incident INC-2026-1767890000: status changed to: mitigated. Monitoring for 60m.

sam (oncall): thanks team. final notes: if any recurrence, escalate to SRE lead and we may enable emergency capacity (burst GPUs) for 30m. Closing active paging.

incident-bot: Incident closed for oncall routing. Please proceed with postmortem and retro. :thumbsup:
